 Anil K.Narendran, J.

 Dated This The 6th Day Of May, 2016
 Judgment

The petitioner, who is running a Small Scale Self Employment Unit, engaged in the business of production and marketing of RO (Reverse Osmosis) Water, has approached this Court in this Writ Petition, seeking a writ of certiorari to quash Ext.P8 prohibitory order dated 16.4.2016 issued by the 1st respondent and for other consequential reliefs.

2. The pleadings and materials on record would show that proceedings were initiated against the petitioner under the provisions of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, alleging that the sample of RO Water taken for analysis is unsafe [Section 3.1 (zz)(iii) and (ix)] and misbranded [Section 3.1(zf)(C)(i)].

Against Ext.P8 prohibitory order issued by the 1st respondent in exercise of his powers under Section 36 (3)(b) and Section 32(3) of the Act, the petitioner filed Ext.P9 appeal before the 2nd respondent under Section 46(4) of the Act.

Now the grievance of the petitioner is that, though Ext.P9 appeal was filed before the 2nd respondent along with an interim prayer to stay the operation of Ext.P8 prohibitory order, the 2nd respondent is yet to take a decision in the matter.

3. I heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned Government Pleader appearing for respondents 1 and 2 and also the learned Assistant Solicitor General of India for the 3rd respondent.

4. Since the petitioner has availed the statutory remedy against Ext.P8 prohibitory order issued by the 1st respondent, the legality or otherwise of the said prohibitory order need not be considered in this Writ Petition and as such, all contentions raised by the petitioner in this regard are left open to be raised before the Appellate Authority, before whom Ext.P9 statutory appeal is pending consideration.

In the result, this Writ Petition is disposed of directing the 2nd respondent to consider and pass appropriate orders on the interim relief sought for in Ext.P9 appeal, as expeditiously as possible, at any rate, within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.

The 2nd respondent shall thereafter pass final orders on Ext.P9 appeal, as expeditiously as possible,
at any rate, within a further period of three months.

Sd/-
